body.box_text: For the latest data about the cost of living and spending read our bulletins on;

body.h4: Largest monthly fall in retail sales since 2021 COVID-19 lockdowns
body.text: Largest monthly fall in retail sales since 2021 COVID-19 lockdowns

body.h4: Largest monthly fall in retail sales since 2021 COVID-19 lockdowns
body.text: [Retail sales volumes](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/retailsalesgreatbritaindecember2023) (the amount of stuff bought) in Great Britain fell by 3.2% in December 2023, the biggest drop since January 2021, when coronavirus (COVID-19) lockdown restrictions were still in place across the country.

body.h4: Largest monthly fall in retail sales since 2021 COVID-19 lockdowns
body.text: The fall follows a 1.4% rise in sales volumes in November 2023. Retailers have suggested that shoppers may have done more of their Christmas shopping in November to take advantage of Black Friday sales.

body.h4: Largest monthly fall in retail sales since 2021 COVID-19 lockdowns
body.text: Annual sales volumes dropped by 2.8% in 2023 reaching the lowest levels since 2018.

body.h4: Largest monthly fall in retail sales since 2021 COVID-19 lockdowns
body.text: Around 6 in 10 adults (62%) in Great Britain said they were spending less on non-essentials because of increases in the cost of living.

body.h4: Largest monthly fall in retail sales since 2021 COVID-19 lockdowns
body.text: This was according to those asked between 17 and 28 January 2024 as part of our latest [Public opinions and social trends bulletin](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/publicopinionsandsocialtrendsgreatbritain17to28january2024).

body.h4: Largest monthly fall in retail sales since 2021 COVID-19 lockdowns
body.text: Overall, around half (49%) of adults said their cost of living had risen compared with a month ago, although this was down from 67% during a similar period a year earlier (11 to 22 January 2023).

body.h4: Largest monthly fall in retail sales since 2021 COVID-19 lockdowns
body.text: According to [more detailed analysis from the survey covering the period 12 July to 1 October 2023](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/impactofincreasedcostoflivingonadultsacrossgreatbritainjulytooctober2023), 3 in 10 adults (29%) said they would not be able to afford an unexpected expense of £850 or more. This rose to 40% among disabled adults, 53% among renters, and 66% among disabled adults who were renting.

body.h4: Largest monthly fall in retail sales since 2021 COVID-19 lockdowns
body.text: Pay growth in real terms (adjusted for inflation) in Great Britain continued to rise in October to December 2023. Annual growth was 1.4% for total pay (including bonuses) and 1.8% for regular pay (excluding bonuses), respectively, according to our [latest earnings data](https://www.ons.gov.uk/employmentandlabourmarket/peopleinwork/employmentandemployeetypes/bulletins/averageweeklyearningsingreatbritain/latest).

body.h4: Largest monthly fall in retail sales since 2021 COVID-19 lockdowns
body.text: By contrast, regular pay growth (not adjusted for inflation and excluding bonuses) remained strong at 6.2% in October to December 2023, but was lower than in recent periods.

body.h4: Largest monthly fall in retail sales since 2021 COVID-19 lockdowns
body.text: Among trading businesses, more than 1 in 6 (18%) expect to increase the price of goods or services they sell in January 2024, according to our latest [Business Insights and Conditions Survey (BICS) for 27 November to 10 December 2023](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/businessinsightsandimpactontheukeconomy14december2023).

body.h4: Largest monthly fall in retail sales since 2021 COVID-19 lockdowns
body.text: Businesses cited energy prices as the main reason for the price increase, at 25%, up 3 percentage points for factors listed for December 2023.
